title: Route apps + discover through the selected daemon/transport path
description:
WHAT: Route every CLI LAN read through the selected path. Two unwired call sites found during 2026-10-14 live verification (binary 92cbdf7, sha256 eec1ea3f...b583cf22):
(a) crates/zestroku-cli/src/apps.rs:112 calls send_selected(AsupersyncTransport, ...) CLI-direct and never consults daemon_client, while sibling read verbs info/active-app route through the daemon (0b162d9). Live result: `apps 192.168.1.182` fails in-pane with EHOSTUNREACH yet exits 0 with a 37-row list via ssh-localhost tree; ZESTROKU_DAEMON_URL has no effect on it.
(b) crates/zestroku-cli/src/devices.rs:133 calls discover(&AsupersyncTransport, ...) directly, bypassing send_selected, so the SSDP/discover path ignores ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=std.
FIX: (a) route apps through daemon_client like info/active-app; (b) route discover through send_selected. No new transport, no second fallback, no stack change.
WHY: `apps` is the only read verb that bypasses the resident-daemon client path (the permanent 8dp fix direction); discover is the only probe that bypasses the env selector. Both are pure wiring.
ACCEPTANCE:
[a] With daemon down, `apps <host>` reports DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE (not EHOSTUNREACH); with daemon up in the ssh tree, exit 0 with app rows. Planted negative: daemon URL pointing at a closed port must refuse as DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE, never silently dial direct.
[b] `ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=std zestroku devices` (SSDP path) honors the selector; planted negative: `ZESTROKU_TRANSPORT=bogus` refuses or falls back deterministically, never silently uses asupersync.
EVIDENCE: live legs 2026-10-14 (devices L1+L2 exit 0, info/active-app exit 0, apps exit 0 via ssh tree / exit 1 in-pane, key denial exit 4 audit 6 zero dispatch); scratch var/agent-tmp/livelegs-local/apps-ssh.out (37 rows), apps.out (exit-1 note).

title: CLI and MCP reach devices through the resident daemon (agent panes cannot open LAN sockets)
description:
WHAT: (a) CLI verbs (devices, info, active-app, apps, key, launch) send to the resident daemon over loopback when it is up and connect directly only with ZESTROKU_DIRECT=1; (b) the MCP stdio server started by an agent is a client of the daemon and opens no LAN socket itself; (c) typed errors: DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE (daemon down: exit within 2 s, no hang) and LAN_BLOCKED_BY_OS_POLICY (a direct connect fails with errno 65 / EHOSTUNREACH while the host answers ping or a platform tool).
WHY: on 2026-10-10 every LAN connect from agent-pane process trees failed with errno 65 while the same binary worked under sshd (measured by PeachKnoll at 22:10Z, reproduced by three agents; mechanism inferred to be macOS Local Network privacy per process tree). An MCP stdio server is spawned by the agent, so it sits in that same blocked tree: a stdio MCP that connects to Rokus itself would be unusable by exactly the agents it is for. The m7c design (c) has this flaw.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] [a] from an agent pane with the daemon up, `zestroku info <express>` exits 0 (live, witness agent); control from the same pane with ZESTROKU_DIRECT=1 exits non-zero with LAN_BLOCKED_BY_OS_POLICY, which shows the daemon path is what made it work.
- [ ] [b] MCP stdio `get_active_app` from the same pane returns the live value; the control direct connect from that pane fails.
- [ ] [a,b] planted negative: stopping the daemon yields DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE within 2 s (test).
- [ ] [c] errno 65 classification unit test with an injected connect error; planted negative: ECONNREFUSED is not classified as policy.
NO-CLAIM: assumes the daemon runs in a tree that holds Local Network permission (resident-daemon bead); says nothing about tailnet access.

title: zestroku doctrine root: owner rules + scope boundary
description:
Root doctrine bead for the zestroku product. Carries the owner rules and the scope boundary every other bead inherits (plan §2/§8):

- Own devices + own LAN only (Express 4K+ .182-class, 50RokuTV .222-class). Never a device the owner does not control.
- Mutations (keypress/launch/install, any settings change) are human-led: one approval per op at point of use. No standing blanket.
- Never commit identifiers (serial/UDN/MAC/ad-id), captures, keys, or firmware images. Fixtures are scrubbed (FIXTURESERIAL-class placeholders).
- Never flash a device. Firmware lane = download + static parse only, offline.
- Documentation-style wording in all instructional text.
- No fuzzing of the shared household LAN in a way that degrades it; cap rates; bench-preferred.
- Shared-tree discipline: Agent Mail reservations before edits; `git commit --only` reserved paths; implementer != verifier (kit-close-needs-evidence).
- Builds/tests via rch (RCH_WORKER=contabo-1 RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1). No darwin workers. CI never needs the network: sim e2e instead.

Acceptance: every other zestroku bead closed with cited evidence; this bead closes last.

title: Human-bound confirmation: tokens an agent cannot mint for itself (bound to device, verb, args, expiry)
description:
WHAT: (a) `zestroku approve <verb> <device> <args...>`, run by the owner, prints a single-use token bound to (device, verb, args, 5-minute expiry); (b) the gate verifies the binding and consumes the token (token store in the action DB); a blank or free-text token, a token for other args or another device, an expired token and a reused token are all refused and audited; (c) `approve` requires an interactive TTY and a typed phrase; in daemon mode the owner approves through an owner-only channel (the loopback web remote or similar): channel choice is an owner decision.
WHY: plan section 1: "an agent doing something careless at 2 a.m. is the failure to design against". Today `--confirm <any non-blank string>` passes (the 2026-10-10 live leg used `--confirm jr`), so an agent can confirm its own mutation; the confirmation is a speed bump, not a guard. The same limit applies to any token that binds bytes but not identity.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] [a] `approve launch <dev> 12` prints a token that the gate accepts for exactly that action once.
- [ ] [b] planted negatives, each exit 4 with a denied audit row and zero POSTs in the request log: the token for 12 used for 13; used for another device; used after expiry (injected clock); used twice; a blank token; a free-text token.
- [ ] [c] `approve` without a TTY refuses with exit 2; the existing `--confirm <anything>` path is removed (planted negative: re-adding it turns a test red).
NO-CLAIM: cannot stop an agent with the same OS account that deliberately drives a TTY (for example tmux send-keys); it stops accidental and self-served confirmations and binds approval to the exact action.

title: CLI --help exits 2 instead of 0
description:
WHAT: `zestroku --help` (and bare `zestroku`) exit 2, so agents checking exit codes misread a successful help render as a usage error. Route `--help`/`-h` to stdout + exit 0; keep unknown subcommands on stderr + exit 2; leave all other exit codes unchanged.

WHY: measured 2026-10-14 on release binary 0e8dca0 (`HELP_EXIT=2`, usage text present); current `main.rs` has no `--help` arm (`None` prints usage to stdout with exit 2, `_` catch-all prints to stderr with exit 2). Exit-code-checking callers (agents, scripts) cannot distinguish help from failure.

ACCEPTANCE:
[a] `zestroku --help` and `zestroku -h` print usage to stdout, exit 0; bare `zestroku` prints usage to stdout, exit 0; unknown subcommand prints usage to stderr, exit 2 (unchanged).
[b] Planted negative: a test asserting exit 2 for `--help` fails after the fix; the committed test pins exit 0 for help and exit 2 for unknown input.
[c] No other CLI exit code changes; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass at the fix SHA.

EVIDENCE: target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/zestroku (`zestroku 0.1.0 0e8dca0`, Mach-O arm64) `--help` output captured with exit 2.

title: M7c: serve daemon — HTTP API + MCP over one asupersync runtime
description:

WHY: M7 of the comprehensive plan (§9) — the product surface. One `Cx` type across daemon/API/MCP/store is the frankensonos dependency-recipe invariant (§3); polling replaces GENA because ECP has no event surface (ECP-WIRE-DOC §5: empty eventSubURLs).
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] (a) `zestroku serve` boots against the real Express and `GET /health` returns 200 from the same asupersync runtime (live leg, Josh present)
- [ ] (b) read routes return live device JSON; a Permissive-tier POST while a device reports Open tier is refused LOCALLY with exit 3 (planted negative: removing the tier check turns that test red)

Cites: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_ZESTROKU.md §3 Surfaces, §9 M7 acceptance; frankensonos §5 Lane D, §7 schema pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] zestroku serve wires discovery -> store -> HTTP API -> MCP under one runtime; SIGTERM shuts down gracefully
- [ ] bind guard refuses 0.0.0.0/wildcard without --allow-unsafe-bind; loopback + LAN binds only
- [ ] MCP stdio echo-tool run proven first (FS:410 precedent); one tool per CLI verb listed via tools/list
- [ ] e2e against zestroku-sim green on rch (no LAN)

1. Acceptance (a) says "live leg, Josh present": the owner said live legs need no presence (2026-10-10); run it through the resident-daemon tree (ssh localhost until the daemon bead lands) with a witness agent.

title: Report serve readiness only after bind and drain on SIGINT
description:

title: M7d: durable store in zestroku-core (tables + migrations + round-trip proof)
description:
Store bead (plan §5 P5 M7d, §3 schema): the durable store in zestroku-core.

Tables (append-only migration list, frankensonos §7 pattern):
- devices(id TEXT PK, name, ip, model, model_num, firmware, wifi_driver, access_tier, last_seen INT)
- apps(device_id, app_id, name, version, fetched_at INT, PK(device_id, app_id))
- capabilities(device_id, cap, PK(device_id, cap))
- access_tier(device_id TEXT PK, tier, probe_at INT, probe_map TEXT) — open/403/404/untested per command class
- actions(id INTEGER PK, at, client, surface, intent, decision, result, before_state) — M4/M7e consumes this
- diff_results(id INTEGER PK, left_device, right_device, surface, field, left_value, right_value, ran_at)

Backend: fsqlite =0.4.9 async-api (the franken-stack pin, DECIDED Josh 2026-10-10). The round-trip proof validates the AsyncConnection shape on the asupersync runtime. Known hazard (frankensonos §4 item 3): fsqlite engine futures overflow a default thread stack — AsyncConnection-style handle or Box::pin on a dedicated 32MiB thread; never a raw !Send future on a default stack. WAL discipline: short transactions, never hold a txn across network I/O.

- [ ] migrations are an append-only numbered list with a schema_migrations table
- [ ] round-trip test: insert/query/update/delete every table in a real temp-file DB (no mocks)
- [ ] backend decision recorded in the bead comment with the proof output
- [ ] identifiers (serial/UDN/MAC/ad-id) never leave the runtime DB into fixtures
## Acceptance Criteria

title: M8: zestroku doctor — check registry + LAN checks
description:
Doctor bead (plan §12.2, frankensonos §12.2 analog): zestroku doctor — what is broken and how to fix it.

Check registry in zestroku-core; each check: id, prerequisites, returns pass/warn/fail/skip with detail + evidence + concrete remedy. Prereq-failed checks skip, not fail.

Checks: data dir + store; SSDP responder per device; targets.toml seeds; each device :8060 device-info fetch + latency; tier posture (probe map re-run, §4 map as structured data); store migrations current; suspend-vs-absent discrimination.

Read-only: never mutates device state. Output: table with remedies or --json; exit 0/6/7 pass/warn/fail. Also MCP doctor and GET /doctor.

- [ ] check registry trait + at least the seven checks above implemented and unit-tested with fixture transports
- [ ] planted negative: a check that mutates state fails review (doctor asserts read-only)
- [ ] exit codes 0/6/7 verified; --json shape documented

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] check registry trait + at least the seven checks above implemented and unit-tested with fixture transports
- [ ] planted negative: a check that mutates state fails review (doctor asserts read-only)
- [ ] exit codes 0/6/7 verified; --json shape documented

## AMENDMENT 2026-10-10 (director, reality-check R1)
Add check `lan-policy` (prereq: at least one seeded or discovered device). It classifies a failed direct connect: errno 65 / EHOSTUNREACH from zestroku while a platform tool answers (`/usr/bin/nc -z -G2 <host> 8060` exits 0) => FAIL with code LAN_BLOCKED_BY_OS_POLICY and remedy "run through the resident daemon (agents) or `ssh -o BatchMode=yes localhost <cmd>`; the macOS Local Network permission of the launching process tree is the suspected gate (inferred, unproven)"; the platform tool also fails => FAIL with code DEVICE_UNREACHABLE (network or device down, not policy).
WHY: a roughly three-hour misdiagnosis on 2026-10-10 (an upstream-library-bug theory, a std-fallback transport, a drafted upstream issue) came from the missing platform-tool control.
ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] `lan-policy` unit-tested with an injected connect error (65) and an injected platform-tool result: policy vs unreachable classified correctly.
- [ ] planted negative: removing the platform-tool control makes both cases classify as policy and the test goes red; ECONNREFUSED is classified as neither.
NO-CLAIM: names the symptom class, not the OS mechanism.

**Principal normalization contract.** Keep transport principal separate from operation `surface`. The current CLI contexts use `client="cli"`; `mcp::decide` uses `client="mcp"` (mcp/lib.rs:104-108), and the current CLI invokes `zestroku_mcp::run_stdio` (main.rs:327; mcp/lib.rs:416-426). A future loopback HTTP mutation adapter must set `loopback-http` explicitly; there are no current HTTP POST routes. MCP currently passes `before_state="unavailable (m7c wires the probe)"` and returns “dispatch happens in serve”; that approval text is not evidence of device execution. HTTP remains read-only. Local token/action/alias/tier-store writes remain distinct from device POSTs. Current MCP registers key/launch only and does not dispatch; current HTTP API has no POST route.

**Future in-tree negatives — UNVERIFIED.** (1) policy denial with a valid token logs `POLICY_DENIED` but leaves `consumed_at` unchanged and sends no device request; (2) unknown principal stays read-only; (3) quiet-hours denial never bypasses per-operation confirmation. No runtime/build claim.

title: Serve startup discovers into an empty DB and preserves inventory across restart
description: Actual startup consumer of shared inventory producer. Existing serve merely opens DB/build_app; externally seeded serve fixtures are NOT discovery proof. Reuse --targets/ZESTROKU_TARGETS/default targets.toml precedence plus --no-ssdp and --mx1..5; one pass, never implicit local /24 fallback or new configuration format. Existing state/transport Arcs shared with unchanged build_app. Pinned fastapi cb9d729 permits on_startup_async only on AppBuilder, NOT returned App: serve integration owner awaits inventory startup after signal registration and before app.run_startup_hooks; Select/drain remains owned by m7c.1.1. Device-info and query/apps observe actual identity/tier using existing classifier/record_probe; do not reclassify status semantics. Persist device first then tier; network outside DB lock; DB persistence failure prevents listening; unreachable discovery retains honest last-known rows without refreshing last_seen. Source startup plan and interfaces from existing devices/core APIs, not new service abstraction. Own serve option/startup hunks and existing serve tests/docs through runtime owner handoff.
acceptance_criteria: [a] Real serve+Permissive/Limited loopback SimDevice, duplicate configured seeds and initially absent DB: health readiness, API exact one row with observed tier BEFORE any info call, reopened Store identity/canonical port/tier data; no devices subprocess or seeded DB. [b] Stop/restart same simulator proves second pass and no duplicates; suspend then restart proves prior model/tier/last_seen durably retained with explicit failed-target note; separate empty DB+suspended sim stays empty. [c] Controlled omission of persistence/identity/tier recording fails independent actual startup assertions while simulator log proves reads; no source-text test or test-only production toggle. LANG:EN — .11.2 startup discovery design note (review only; no source edits).

Current seam: origin/main serve.rs:45-48 registers SIGTERM then runs App startup hooks; run() opens the store at :96 and builds the shared API app at :103, with no discovery. `devices.rs:35-55,81-83,112-134` already establishes the target semantics: `ZESTROKU_TARGETS` default, `--targets` override, default `~/.config/zestroku/targets.toml` via inventory::read_seeds, `--no-ssdp` seed-only, and `--mx` 1..=5 (default 3). Reuse inventory.rs:34-70 and core ssdp_io::discover; do not add a config format, private /24 fallback, subprocess, runtime, schema, or second discovery service.

Proposed lifecycle: extend serve options only with `--targets`, `--no-ssdp`, and `--mx`; open the DB once, retain the same `Arc<Mutex<SqliteStore>>` and transport for unchanged `build_app`, and pass that same state to a small local startup step. In the existing async serve entry, register SIGTERM first, then await exactly one discovery/inventory pass before `app.run_startup_hooks` and before binding/listening. `--no-ssdp` uses `inventory::seeds_only`; otherwise call `ssdp_io::discover(transport, seeds, mx)`. Network calls occur outside the DB mutex. Persist each successful `(Device, identity)` through `inventory::persist_inventory` under a short lock; identity moves/aliases remain producer-owned. If persistence errors, fail startup before hooks/listener.

After the device row exists, issue the existing read-only `query/apps` probe outside the DB lock, use the existing `classify_tier_from_response` and `record_probe` path (CLI precedent main.rs:213-228), then lock only to record the observation. Do not invent tier semantics or record an unobserved tier. This ordering makes the row, canonical endpoint, identity, and observed tier durable before readiness; `/info` is not required to seed tier.

No responders / suspended target is degraded discovery, not a fabricated success: preserve last-known rows and tier, do not refresh `last_seen` for failed targets, and do not delete inventory. Emit the failed-target note; with an empty DB remain empty. Continue serving health and last-known rows if the DB is healthy. Invalid seed/configuration and DB/persistence failures fail startup. Keep the existing serve Select/drain implementation owned by m7c.1.1; signal registration remains before discovery.

Acceptance proof: real serve binary + loopback SimDevice and fresh DB with duplicate seeds; poll health then `/v1/devices` before `/info`, require exactly one canonical row with actual tier and reopen Store to check identity/port/tier. Restart same DB and prove no duplicate. Suspend then restart and require unchanged model/tier/last_seen plus explicit failed-target note; separate fresh DB+suspended target stays empty. A planted omission of identity/persistence/tier recording must fail those real API/store assertions while the simulator log shows actual `device-info` and `apps` reads. Preserve drain assertions while accounting for these startup probes. Loopback/seed tests prove no household multicast success.

title: MCP key/launch execute approved mutations through resident daemon, never approval-only success
description:
WHAT: Wire the existing stdio MCP key and launch mutation tools through the configured loopback resident-daemon client and the existing inventory-selected HTTP mutation routes. Forward the opaque owner approval token for the daemon to verify and consume atomically; never consume approval in MCP and then return success without device dispatch. No direct LAN path, URL supplied by tool arguments, or fallback on daemon failure. Keep read-only list_devices/info/active_app/apps behavior and the accepted .11.4 contract unchanged. Reuse the pinned fastmcp/asupersync client seam; no nested runtime, dependency, unsafe code, or protocol reconstruction.

WHY: Existing MCP key/launch handlers can report approval without dispatch. Agents run in a process tree that cannot open Roku LAN sockets; control must flow through the resident daemon. This leaf is intentionally separate from .11.4 read-only tool consumers and depends on the HTTP key/launch routes in .11.3.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) Real MCP stdio -> real loopback daemon -> SimDevice key and launch each cause exactly one device mutation and corresponding state transition. (b) The daemon creates one shared audited completed action with the actual before-state, selected target, approval result, and actual outcome; ECP/device failure is recorded as failure, never success. (c) Missing, blank, invalid, expired, replayed, and wrong-target tokens cause zero mutation POSTs; tool response is an error/refusal, never approval-only success. (d) Unavailable daemon returns a tool error, does not consume approval, and causes no direct ECP request or fallback. (e) Planted negative: restoring gate-only approval success fails the state/audit outcome contract. (f) Preserve .11.4 read-tool scope and acceptance without changing its read behavior; do not claim live owner mutation from simulator evidence. (g) Verify pinned async handler seam, use strict remote source-bound tests and required project gates with no skips, actual-binary MCP smoke, and a nonauthor receipt.
acceptance_criteria: Real stdio MCP key and launch reach the resident daemon and cause exactly one SimDevice state change; daemon audit records the actual before-state and completed outcome; all invalid, expired, replayed, and wrong-target approval tokens dispatch zero mutations; daemon-down returns an error with no token consumption or direct-LAN fallback; ECP failure is audited as failure; planted approval-only success fails behavior assertions; .11.4 read-only contract remains unchanged; strict remote tests and required gates pass with no skips and actual binary smoke plus nonauthor receipt.

title: zestroku RCH pooled targets regrow ~12-21 GB per root per worker within hours and starve all Contabo workers: owner policy + measured growth
description:
WHAT: zestroku's own RCH pooled targets regrow to about 12-21 GB per root per worker within hours of building, which keeps filling every Contabo worker: contabo-1 refilled 44.1 GB free (06:40Z after reclaim) to 10.3 GB (07:39Z); contabo-4 refilled from 29.1 GB (07:47Z) to 12.9 GB (09:36Z). rch gc cannot reap them (pooled window 24 h, no flag to shorten). The reclaim route that works is native: drain, rch gc preview, apply only COLLECT, enable, probe (ompkit-wjbk, ev_c0f1ec64289a6035).
MEASURED 2026-10-13 09:36Z (rch cache status, rc 0): per worker TWO zestroku pooled stores plus a cargo cache: contabo-1: Developer/zestroku pool 16715 MB + rch-build/rch-remote/zestroku pool 21245 MB + cargo cache 1064 MB = 39025 MB, 0 reapable. contabo-4: Developer/zestroku pool 11994 MB + rch-build pool 13274 MB + cache 4897 MB = 30166 MB. contabo-2: zestroku Developer pool 6583 MB (4h idle) + others. Reading: a plain rch exec fills the Developer/zestroku pool, a clean-overlay run fills the rch-build/.../zestroku pool, so using both modes costs two pools per worker. NOT measured: growth per run, or whether pools are reused across different --base shas (an earlier guess of per-sha pools was refuted: same hash names reappeared).
WHY: contabo-1/-2/-3 sit at 0 slots on disk; contabo-4 (8 GB RAM) is the only worker that can run a job, and OOM-killed rustc three times today (kernel log, see AM 52352). Capacity is the binding constraint on every zestroku gate.
ASK (owner decision, not a code change): choose and record a policy: (1) clean-overlay only for proofs, plain runs only for scratch checks, so one pool per worker; (2) a cap or a scheduled sequenced reclaim for zestroku pools after each proof batch (sanctioned route only: drain, preview, apply COLLECT, enable, probe); (3) ask the RCH owner for a shorter pooled window or a per-project cap (rch gc has no such option today). Not proposed: deleting pools by hand, bypassing rch gc, or weakening any gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] [a] A written policy (one of 1-3 above or a better one) lives in AGENTS.md or a bead comment and workers cite it in receipts.
- [ ] [b] Measured: after one full proof batch (SIGTERM + workspace + Clippy, -j1) on one worker, record rch cache status before and after so the pool growth per batch is a number, not a guess.
- [ ] [c] Planted negative: a policy that allows both plain and clean-overlay runs on the same worker must be shown to produce two pooled stores on that worker (cache status), i.e. the one-pool claim is checked, not assumed.
- [x] [d] Disk of every worker that carries slots stays above the RCH warning threshold across the next batch, read from rch status, or the bead states why not.
